title: Shell Norco C2 splitter PV-1767: +25 % ethylene (real plant, 2015 revamp)
source: Summers, de Villiers and Green, Chemical Engineering Transactions 69 (2018) 703-708, DOI 10.3303/CET1869118 (Sulzer and Shell): operating data before the revamp (April 2015); the revamp itself is withheld
question: The feed will shift to about 69 wt % ethylene and the unit needs about 25 % more ethylene from this tower at polymer-grade purity. What limits the C2 splitter, and what is the change?
data_note: Real plant: Shell's Norco C2 splitter, with operating data and tray hydraulics from the published paper (April 2015, before the revamp). The paper normalises flows to a 1,000 kg/h feed; PlantAgent assumes absolute flow = normalised x 92, backed out from the paper's 87 % jet flood at 4,877 mm. What Shell actually did is withheld from the agent and shown only in the comparison. The featured loop (Muse Spark Open, one round) re-trays the same shell; the server verified 125 % with the ethylene product at 1.26x today, flood 75 % of the 85 % limit, ethane 0 ppm, and P(target) 100 % of 39 solved samples. The new tray rating is the agent's assumption (vendor to confirm), the feed was solved at today's composition rather than the 69 wt % premise, and the feed-tray move Shell made was not proposed.
suggested_questions: What limits the tower at the new feed?
What change reaches +25 % ethylene at polymer grade?
Which tower section is closest to flooding?
What happens to the condenser and reboiler duties?
